_comment: Every [TWEAK] value from GAME_DESIGN.md lives here. Section refs point to the design doc. Values marked placeholder in _comment are not specified by the doc.

performance._comment: §30.1, §30.2. Pass criterion p95 <= budget chosen by the user 2026-09-30. Thread/chunk/benchmark settings are engineering defaults.
performance._pathing_comment: Phase 1 1a: after a map change, flow fields are updated on background threads and swapped in exactly pathing_rebuild_latency_ticks later (the sim waits if they aren't ready), so results never depend on timing. 24 ticks = one in-game day: a new path is used from the next day, like a short construction job; an update takes ~0.1 s, well under the 2 s a game day lasts at 1x. benchmark_edit_every_ticks toggles a path tile in the benchmark to exercise this.

map._comment: §5.1, §12.1: buildings rotate in 15-degree steps (resolved in GAME_DESIGN.md v0.4).

needs._comment: §10.1, §32. Weights are from §32. initial range, baseline_per_hour (negative = decay, positive = recovery) and activity_effects (per in-game hour) are placeholders (not in the doc).

walking._comment: §12.4 (v0.4): students prefer paved paths and cut across grass only when it saves enough. Placeholders, tuned in Phase 1 1b: with grass 1.25x and a 15 m penalty for leaving a path (paid half on the way off, half on the way back), cutting diagonally across a lawn pays off from roughly 70 m sides (a big quad), not for small lawns or corner-trimming. Rough ground (fields, pasture, woods) costs 3x, so people keep to roads outside town. Commute need drops per minute walked.

desire_paths._comment: A lawn/rough tile crossed by at least min_walkers_per_day people that day wears 1/days_to_wear; otherwise it grows back 1/days_to_regrow. Fully worn = a desire path (dirt). 'Grass wears to dirt over weeks' (§12.4).

retention._comment: §32: R = base + happiness*H/100 + gpa*GPA/4 + belonging*B/100 - financial_stress*FS/100, clamped

teaching_identity._comment: §13.7. Sweet spot 55-80 is LOCKED; stored here so code never hard-codes it.
